drugs.name: Larazotide Acetate (AT-1001)
drugs.mechanism: Tight junction regulator and zonulin antagonist preventing gluten-induced opening of intestinal epithelial tight junctions
drugs.efficacy: Reduces abdominal symptoms and paracellular gluten peptide permeation in patients on gluten-free diet
drugs.adverse_effects: Headache, nausea, abdominal discomfort (generally placebo-level tolerability)

drugs.name: Latiglutenase (ALV003)
drugs.mechanism: Combination of two gluten-specific proteases (cysteine endoprotease and prolyl endopeptidase) degrading toxic immunogenic gluten peptides in stomach
drugs.efficacy: Protects intestinal mucosa and reduces symptoms following accidental gluten exposure in celiac disease

drugs.name: Dapsone
drugs.mechanism: Anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial agent inhibiting neutrophil myeloperoxidase and migration in dermatitis herpetiformis
drugs.efficacy: Rapid resolution of intensely pruritic skin lesions within 24 to 48 hours in celiac-associated dermatitis herpetiformis
drugs.adverse_effects: Dose-dependent hemolysis, methemoglobinemia, agranulocytosis, peripheral neuropathy

drugs.name: Budesonide (Enteric-coated)
drugs.mechanism: High first-pass hepatic metabolism glucocorticoid suppressing mucosal inflammation in upper gastrointestinal tract
drugs.approval: Standard of Care (for Refractory Celiac Disease Type 1)
drugs.efficacy: Induces histological and clinical remission in steroid-responsive refractory celiac disease
drugs.adverse_effects: Mild Cushingoid effects, headache, dyspepsia, adrenal suppression at high doses
